note: scripts/check-single-entry.ts: per rule, the files where the pattern may appear, the count each may hold, and why the file is right. A count only goes down; UNREVIEWED is the seeding's placeholder for a file nobody has read yet.

src/routes/organisms/workspace-ops.ts.why: A shared workspace link's own password, not an account's: there is no account to lock, and the unlock route limits attempts to 10 per 15 minutes per address.

src/services/password-check.ts.why: The one check: checkPassword applies the account lock and the attempt count around it.

src/services/owner-erasure.ts.why: eraseOwner, the one account deletion: it clears what the storage cascade does not reach, then runs the cascade.

src/index.ts.why: The command line's seed command reads this node's own admin answer over localhost. Backup and restore moved to cli/backup-restore.ts, which reads under a ceiling (2026-10-16).

src/services/ai/fetch.ts.why: request.arrayBuffer() reads the outgoing request this node built, not an answer.

src/utils/logger.ts.why: winston.format.json() is a log format, not a body read.

src/middleware/rate-limit.ts.why: The rate multiplier of the operator's own session. The operator's agent keeps an agent's rate.

src/routes/access-tokens.ts.why: Whether a new personal token may carry the operator role: a role is granted, never inherited at mint time, so only the operator in person may mint one.

src/routes/agents/management.ts.why: C4: asks whether the session is the account holder in person, not whether it is the operator. Moves to isOwnerInPerson.

src/routes/memory/key.ts.why: Reads the role list the route built with rolesWithOperator, which asked askOperator.

src/services/agent-proposals.ts.why: C4: asks whether the session is the account holder in person. Moves to isOwnerInPerson.

src/services/board-post.ts.why: Reads the caller's role list, which both surfaces build from askOperator (rolesWithOperator on REST, boardCaller on MCP).

src/services/board-write.ts.why: Reads the caller's role list, which both surfaces build from askOperator (rolesWithOperator on REST, boardCaller on MCP).

src/services/caller-facts.ts.why: readerOf: an unattended run is ['operator'] without 'owner' and reads as an AI; the reader kind is not the operator question isOperatorCaller answers (moved from classification/reader-kind.ts, codebase analysis 2026-11-03, B1).

src/services/consent-write.ts.why: C4: asks whether the session is the account holder in person. Moves to isOwnerInPerson.

src/services/group-shares.ts.why: C4: asks whether the session is the account holder in person. Moves to isOwnerInPerson.

src/services/memory-write.ts.why: C4: asks whether the session is the account holder in person. Moves to isOwnerInPerson.

src/services/operator-principal.ts.why: askOperator itself: the operator in person is read off the session's roles.

src/services/owner-mailbox-reads.ts.why: C4: asks whether the session is the account holder in person. Moves to isOwnerInPerson.

src/services/datapackage/odata.ts.why: An XML escaper for the OData CSDL document, not HTML: it writes the XML entity ' for ', which XML defines and HTML 4 does not. It escapes all five characters.

src/services/finance/finvoice.ts.why: An XML escaper for the Finvoice 3.0 document a bank channel reads, not HTML. A ' in element text or a double-quoted attribute needs no escape in XML, and the E2E golden-file suite holds the document byte for byte, so it keeps its four-character escape.

src/models/signal-schemas.ts.why: STREAM_ID_RE: a signal stream's id, not an agent name.

src/routes/organisms/intake.ts.why: FORM_ID_RE: an intake form's id, not an agent name.

src/commerce/agent-purchase-limit.ts.why: Asks whether the caller is an agent (agent role and no owner role), which the limit is about.

src/middleware/rate-limit.ts.why: The rate multiplier per role, not an access decision.

src/routes/agents/device-auth.ts.why: The device-auth approver's kind (autoApprovePrincipal), which picks the approval path by role.

src/routes/agents/management.ts.why: (owner || operator) without agent or ecosystem: also admits the node's own operator-only caller (system runs build roles ['operator']), which isOwnerInPerson refuses.

src/routes/ghii/owner-session.ts.why: Reads the stored account record's roles to mint a sign-in token, not a session's.

src/routes/mcp-servers.ts.why: Sets the callerKind label in a record; decides nothing.

src/routes/schemas.ts.why: The owner role or the operator (isOperatorCaller) may define a schema: a role test, not the in-person question.

src/routes/skills.ts.why: Asks whether the caller is an agent session.

src/routes/wallet.ts.why: Asks whether the caller is an agent session.

src/services/agent-proposals.ts.why: (owner || operator) without agent: also admits the node's own operator-only caller, which isOwnerInPerson refuses.

src/services/caller-facts.ts.why: readerOf tells a person from an AI by the roles (an app and a visitor count as a person there, which isOwnerInPerson does not answer), and credentialVia names a signed-in session; neither decides access (moved from classification/reader-kind.ts, codebase analysis 2026-11-03, B1).

src/services/consent-write.ts.why: (owner || operator) without agent: also admits the node's own operator-only caller, which isOwnerInPerson refuses.

src/services/external-login.ts.why: Reads the stored account record's roles to mint a sign-in token, not a session's.

src/services/group-shares.ts.why: (owner || operator) without agent: also admits the node's own operator-only caller, which isOwnerInPerson refuses.

src/services/memory-write.ts.why: (owner || operator) without agent: also admits the node's own operator-only caller, which isOwnerInPerson refuses.

src/services/notification-create.ts.why: Asks whether the caller is an agent session.

src/services/operator-principal.ts.why: askOperator itself: whether a role list acts for someone.

src/services/owner-mailbox-reads.ts.why: (owner || operator) when nothing acts for someone: also admits the node's own operator-only caller, which isOwnerInPerson refuses.

src/services/extension-network-hosts.ts.why: Not a scope test: both refuse a hostname wildcard (*.example.com), in a manifest host and in a host field value, because hosts are compared exactly. Moved from extension-manifest.ts with hostRefusal() on 2026-10-09.

src/mcp/commerce.ts.why: The claims of a token being minted, not a caller. The role list stays literal so this mint can be diffed against the other mints (security.md: a role is granted, never inherited at mint time).

src/mcp/oauth.ts.why: The claims an OAuth authorization code carries until the token endpoint mints them; an Express router with no MCP session and no caller yet.

src/mcp/tool-usage-wrap.ts.why: The refusal log entry written by the wrapper around every MCP tool; the wrapper is installed before the tool groups and holds only the session's GAII.

src/routes/agents-v2/enrolment.ts.why: The claims of a token being minted, not a caller. The role list stays literal so this mint can be diffed against the other mints (security.md: a role is granted, never inherited at mint time).

src/routes/agents-v2/token.ts.why: The claims of a token being minted, not a caller. The role list stays literal so this mint can be diffed against the other mints (security.md: a role is granted, never inherited at mint time).

src/routes/agents/device-auth-approve.ts.why: The claims of a token being minted, not a caller. The role list stays literal so this mint can be diffed against the other mints (security.md: a role is granted, never inherited at mint time). The mint moved here from device-auth.ts on 2026-10-20 (max-file-lines).

src/routes/auth.ts.why: The claims of a token being minted, not a caller. The role list stays literal so this mint can be diffed against the other mints (security.md: a role is granted, never inherited at mint time). This one is the anonymous-mode token.

src/routes/upload.ts.why: A presigned upload token carries no roles or scopes, so the operator question is asked of the principal it names, with the scopes its agent record holds now.

src/services/chat-agent.ts.why: The claims of a token being minted, not a caller. The role list stays literal so this mint can be diffed against the other mints (security.md: a role is granted, never inherited at mint time).

src/services/classification/reader.ts.why: readerForAgent, the reader for MCP call sites that hold only the agent's GAII. The reader reads no scopes; it moves onto caller() when those call sites do.

src/services/operator-principal.ts.why: resolveOperatorAgentName, the operator answer for MCP call sites that hold the agent's GAII and the session scopes (admin-*.ts and others); it moves onto caller().operator() when those call sites do. One count is the @usage line.

src/routes/ghii/attach-email.ts.why: Not a mail gate: an account already at level 1 or above has nothing to complete, so the sign-in's attach-email step answers ALREADY_VERIFIED. The code it sends goes to the address the person types in this request.

src/routes/ghii/register-login.ts.why: Not a mail gate: the sign-in refusal EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED on a node that requires a confirmed address (email_confirmation_required) asks whether the account was ever verified; it sends no mail.

src/services/login-link.ts.why: Not a mail gate: after a sign-in link is spent, an account below level 1 is raised to level 1. The link opens only while the address it was mailed to is still the account's (stillTheirs).

src/routes/openrouter.ts.why: The legacy settings route (GET /v1/openrouter/settings says whether the record holds a key, and the model list decrypts it to ask the provider's catalogue); neither decides who pays for a completion.

src/services/notebook-ai.ts.why: resolveOwnerModel reads the record only to say whether the person's own key pays and which model they chose; a person with no key of their own is asked of prepareAiCall.

src/services/own-key-coverage.ts.why: hasOwnAiKey, the one answer to whether a person has an AI key of their own: it reads the legacy record beside the provider keys.

src/index-start.ts.why: The boot generates a random admin password when none is configured and writes it into the config; nothing is compared.

src/index.ts.why: The `aimeat seed` command sends the configured admin password to the node's own seed-examples route as a client; the node checks it with checkAdminPassword.

src/services/admin-password.ts.why: checkAdminPassword, the one compare, with the count of wrong passwords per address.

src/utils/env-config/sections-node.ts.why: The configuration display shows the password masked, or says it is generated at start; nothing is compared.

src/commerce/settle-purchase.ts.why: The one booking step: the fee record and the beneficiary shares, inside the purchase's transaction.

src/services/config-apply.ts.why: The one writer and the one reset: storeConfigValue and resetConfigValue, behind the tighten-only rule of applyConfigChanges and resetRefusal.

src/services/config-at-rest-rows.ts.why: The start-up pass that encrypts a secret row stored in plain text: it rewrites the same value sealed, so no setting changes and there is no caller.

src/services/hooks-overview.ts.why: The hooks.<name> rows hold the operator's hook lists, which are not Config rows (no row in config-schema.ts), so no setting rule applies. setHookActions is reached from PUT and DELETE /v1/admin/hooks/:hookName (requireOperator) and the MCP admin hooks tool (operator test); the other writes are start-up migrations.

src/services/owner-session.ts.why: settleRefreshCookieWindowAtStart stores auth.refresh_cookie_legacy_until once at start when no source set it: the node's own write, no caller, and the row has no tighten-only rule.

src/services/app-artifact-lint.ts.why: The publish-time asset probe (probeOne) and the cortex lib read (readNodeLib): anonymous server-side GETs of the node's own served paths, with appAssetProbe off in tests. Not a headless browser, as the codebase analysis listed them; they could take the in-process dispatch too, which D-j did not include.

src/services/app-playtest.ts.why: The headless browser loads the app page from this origin, and the page's relative URLs resolve against it; a browser needs a real socket.

src/services/connect-tunnel.ts.why: loopbackBase: the origin a tunnel frame's path is resolved against and pinned to (the SSRF guard in connect-tunnel-forward.ts). No request goes to it over a socket: the forward is dispatched in process.

src/services/design-book/bench.ts.why: The headless browser loads the bench page from this origin, and the kit's relative assets resolve against it; a browser needs a real socket.

src/services/headless-network.ts.why: The headless browser's own-origin list, and the base from which the node fetches (through safeFetch) what that browser asks of the node's own pages. Part of the headless rendering the codebase analysis left on the socket.

src/routes/agents-v2/enrolment.ts.why: A MINT: the enrolled credential adds the store place's default on the agent's first time (widenAndAnnounce). Moving it to approval changes which agents get the default (B7 report); it stays here until the developer rules.

src/routes/agents-v2/token.ts.why: A MINT: the crew run's token adds the store place's default on the agent's first time (widenAndAnnounce). Moving it to approval changes which agents get the default (B7 report); it stays here until the developer rules.

src/routes/agents/device-auth-approve.ts.why: THE APPROVAL: the owner, or an agent within its own scopes, approves the agent and the place's default is written to its record there (applyPlaceDefault with the approver's bound). This is where the decision belongs.

src/routes/auth.ts.why: MINTS: POST /v1/auth/token (an agent's signed challenge) and POST /v1/auth/refresh (an agent session) add the store place's default on the agent's first time (widenAndAnnounce). Moving them to approval changes which agents get the default (B7 report); they stay here until the developer rules.

src/mcp/commerce.ts.why: The fulfilment call's token for the calling agent itself: its own sub and role, the scopes on its record.

src/mcp/oauth.ts.why: MCP OAuth code exchange and refresh: the agent the owner chose on the consent page, the scopes on its record, the roles the code carried.

src/routes/access-tokens.ts.why: A JWT exchanged from a personal access token: the PAT row's sub, roles and (for an agent-level PAT) scopes, marked via pat.

src/routes/admin.ts.why: The setup session after the admin password: the owner record's own roles, no scopes.

src/routes/agents-v2/enrolment.ts.why: The enrolled agent's credential: role agent, the scopes on its record (with the store place's default, see scope-widen-at-mint).

src/routes/agents-v2/token.ts.why: A crew run's token from a signed assertion: role agent, the scopes on its record (with the store place's default, see scope-widen-at-mint).

src/routes/agents/device-auth-approve.ts.why: Device authorization approved: role agent, the scopes granted at this approval.

src/routes/app-grants.ts.why: An app grant's access token: role app, the scopes the owner approved for the grant, the app named.

src/routes/auth.ts.why: Anonymous mode's token (ANONYMOUS_SCOPES); an agent's signed challenge (its record's scopes, with the place default); the deprecated owner-key sign-in (owner record roles); a PAT cookie refresh (the PAT row); POST /v1/auth/refresh (the same roles and the record's scopes again).

src/routes/ecosystem-apps.ts.why: An ecosystem app approved by its owner: role ecosystem, the scopes approved.

src/routes/ghii/register-login.ts.why: Registration (the owner record's roles, or owner) and the federated sign-in (role federated, the visitor's home name, the peer's granted scopes).

src/routes/ghii/web-verify.ts.why: The agent created by a web identity proof: role agent, the scopes on its record.

src/routes/setup.ts.why: The first owner's session at node setup: the owner record's own roles.

src/services/chat-agent.ts.why: The node chat's own agent (mintChatAgentToken): role agent, the scopes of its identity, an MCP or REST audience.

src/services/owner-session.ts.why: The owner's access token at sign-in and at the two refresh-cookie steps: the owner's current roles, no scopes.

src/cli/connect/agent-key.ts.why: The connector signs its agent's own assertion with the agent's own key; the node verifies it with the public key on the agent's record.

src/services/agent-card.ts.why: The signed agent card: a JWS that callers outside the node verify with the published key, so it is signed with that key.

src/services/dataspace/identity.ts.why: The dataspace identity token: other participants verify it with the node's published JWK (routes/dsp/index.ts), so it keeps the node key.

src/services/dataspace/presentation.ts.why: Verifies a verifiable presentation and its credentials with the keys their outside issuers publish.

src/services/dataspace/verifier.ts.why: Verifies another dataspace participant's self-issued token with that participant's own key.

src/services/docsign/eudi.ts.why: The request object to an EUDI wallet, signed with the signing credential's own key and certificate chain.

src/services/sd-jwt.ts.why: Verifies an outside issuer's SD-JWT with that issuer's key.

src/services/vc-issuer.ts.why: A verifiable credential: holders and verifiers outside the node check it against the node's DID key, so it is signed and verified with the node key.
